Microbial pathogen.requires: faecal or environmental ingress and survivable conditions
Microbial pathogen.provides: acute illness within days, killed by chlorine, detectable by culture

Heavy metal leaching.requires: corrosive water in contact with metal pipe or solder
Heavy metal leaching.provides: chronic exposure, no taste at low levels, unaffected by disinfection

Industrial solvent ingress.requires: a spill reaching the source or a permeable main
Industrial solvent ingress.provides: distinctive odour at low concentration, chronic toxicity, not removed by chlorination

Disinfection byproduct.requires: chlorine reacting with natural organic matter
Disinfection byproduct.provides: formed by the treatment itself, chronic risk only, rises with treatment intensity

Source reservoir.requires: contamination of the raw water body
Source reservoir.provides: whole-supply exposure, treatment has a chance to remove it

Treatment plant failure.provides: everything downstream affected, detectable at plant outlet

Distribution main breach.requires: a pressure loss or physical break
Distribution main breach.provides: localised ingress to one zone, no plant indication

Household plumbing.requires: materials or conditions inside one property
Household plumbing.provides: single-property exposure, invisible to any utility monitoring

Routine compliance sampling.provides: detection days later, statutory parameters only

Continuous chlorine residual monitor.provides: immediate indication of disinfection loss, blind to anything not consuming chlorine

Consumer taste and odour complaint.requires: a perceptible change and a consumer reporting it
Consumer taste and odour complaint.provides: rapid unstructured signal, only for perceptible contaminants

Clinical case cluster.requires: people falling ill and being linked
Clinical case cluster.provides: detection only after harm, days to weeks of delay

Boil water notice.provides: immediate protection from microbes, useless against chemicals

Flush and rechlorinate mains.requires: network access and a chlorine-susceptible contaminant
Flush and rechlorinate mains.provides: removal from the distribution system, days of work

Switch to alternative source.provides: elimination of a source-side problem, no effect on distribution or household issues

Point-of-use filtration.provides: protection of one property, unscalable to a city

Single building.requires: an issue confined to one property
Single building.provides: small affected population, property-level remedies feasible

One distribution zone.requires: a contaminant confined by network geometry

Entire city.provides: whole population affected, no unaffected zone to switch to

_v1_notes.CONTAMINANT|ENTRY POINT: heavy metal leaching is Y only at household plumbing - it is a pipe-material phenomenon. Disinfection byproducts are formed by treatment, so Y only at the treatment plant. Microbial and solvent ingress are N at household plumbing.
_v1_notes.CONTAMINANT|DETECTION: chlorine residual monitors detect only chlorine-consuming contamination, so N for metals, solvents and byproducts. Taste and odour is N for microbes and metals at low levels, Y for solvents. Clinical clusters are N for chronic contaminants - metals, solvents and byproducts do not produce an acute cluster.
_v1_notes.CONTAMINANT|RESPONSE: boiling is useless against every chemical contaminant, so Y only for microbes. Rechlorination is N for metals. Alternative source is N for household plumbing issues but that is the entry-point pairing; here metals are Y since a less corrosive source helps.
_v1_notes.CONTAMINANT|POPULATION AFFECTED: heavy metal leaching is N for one zone and N for an entire city - it is property-specific.
_v1_notes.ENTRY POINT|DETECTION: household plumbing is N for continuous chlorine monitoring, which is not installed inside properties.
_v1_notes.ENTRY POINT|RESPONSE: distribution main breach is N for switching source. Household plumbing is N for boiling, flushing and source switching alike - only point-of-use filtration reaches it.
